Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Please find a concise package below; attached are three artifacts and a short runbook excerpt. Ive summarized the operational controls up front so your team can land this in procurement quickly.

Executive summary (short):
- EU data processing: Redwood processes customer data in the region(s) selected by the customer. For Hosted and Dedicated customers choosing EU region, inference compute and KV caches remain in-region. For hybrid Dedicated/private deployments where routing is customer-controlled, cross-border processing only occurs when explicitly configured or when customer requests cross-region fallbacks; such behavior is covered by SCCs and our DPA annex.
- Safeguards: SCCs (EU Commission clauses) + DPA annex in place. Customer-managed KMS via Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated customers via HSM-backed KMS integrations; default rotation policy is 90 days, configurable.
- Subprocessors and routing: runtime subprocessors and cloud partners used for control-plane coordination are listed in the attached subprocessor PDF and are contractually bounded by our DPA.

Attachments (attached):
- redwood-dpf-ops-evidence.pdf (procedures & runbook excerpts, dated 2026-08-06)
- dpa-annex-current.pdf (redline-ready DPA annex version 3.2)
- subprocessor-list-202608.pdf (current subprocessors for runtime + infra)
- kv-cache-residency-runbook.md (runbook excerpt for KV/prefix cache residency and eviction logic)

Quick answers to your numbered asks:
1) Cross-border handling & KV caches: By default, KV/prefix caches are colocated with inference pods in the same region for Hosted and Dedicated EU deployments. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers the KV cache can be configured to remain on customer-managed infrastructure; our runbook excerpt describes the default agent behavior and configuration knobs.
2) EU->US processing statement: Redwood does not transfer EU personal data to the US for inference workloads when a customer has selected EU region-only hosting or Private on-prem. If cross-region fallbacks are enabled by the customer, transfers are executed under the SCCs and contractual safeguards noted in the DPA annex.
3) Artifacts: linked in this email as attachments and in Drive (see link).

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-redwood-mednova-dpf (read-only)

Hi Sarah — quick technical clarifications below (pulled from the attached runbook section 2.3 and 4.1).

1) Key rotation (BYOK):
   - Customer-driven rotation without downtime: supported. Our key architecture allows the customer to rotate keys in their KMS (or HSM) and present a new key-version to Redwood via the KMS connector. During rotation, Redwood maintains a dual-key acceptance window where both old and new key-versions are valid for decryption to allow in-flight sessions to complete. This is orchestrated via our control-plane KMS connector (no manual data re-encryption required) and is designed to avoid service disruption. See runbook: kv-cache-residency-runbook.md, section "KMS rotation and acceptance window" (page 4).

2) KV cache residency for Private + cross-region failover:
   - Default behaviour: when Private is configured with cross-region failover enabled, cache shards are first attempted to be rehydrated from customer VPC subnets within the failover region (if customer has set up a secondary VPC endpoint). If the customer has not provisioned a secondary VPC endpoint, Redwood will not automatically replicate persistent KV caches to Redwood-managed fallbacks for Private deployments unless explicitly consented in writing; ephemeral caches may be served from a Redwood-managed read-only fallback in the configured fallback region for short-lived session continuity (TTL-driven).
   - Explicit statement: Persistent KV/prefix caches for Private deployments remain under customer control unless customer signs an ops exception allowing Redwood-managed replication out-of-region. See runbook: kv-cache-residency-runbook.md, sections "Failover cache policy" and "Customer-managed replication" (pages 2-6).

If you want, we can redact and extract the two short paragraphs above into a one-page statement that procurement can insert directly into the security appendix.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security Operations
Redwood Inference
